fields.description:
## Context / Problem

The completion verifier receives only the fenced ticket_context (description + comments, gate_ops.py assemble step) — zero file contents. Every file is discovered agentically: measured across five live verifier runs, 84-158 requests x ~4-6s each, dominated by read_file/search_files round-trips, and all four captured runaway loops were search_files repeat signatures — the model hunting for text it expects to exist. Wall-clock cost is round-trips, not tokens: runs already cache-read 8.7M of 8.8M input tokens, but that history was assembled one tool round-trip at a time. Overlap analysis of the four live gate traces against the closing subtree's file_impact union shows 67-82% of distinct file reads are covered by declared file_impact — the verifier spends its opening requests re-fetching files the tickets already name.

## Approach

PRE-FETCH, do not restrict (operator-ratified direction): append a bounded, clearly-labelled prefetched-content section to the byte-stable leading part of the fenced verifier context — the ticket's declared file_impact contents plus the referencing commits' diffs — while keeping the full tool surface untouched so the agent still explores beyond the prefetch. Assistance, not a ceiling.

### Which file_impact set each entrypoint prefetches (close gate is graph=False)

The completion CLOSE gate (`_commands.transition`) passes `graph=False` (gate_ops.py:133, gate_dispatch.py:535): an epic close verifies its OWN completion criteria, not its whole descendant subtree — re-deriving graph here was the removed runaway bug that blew the step budget (gate_ops.py:138-140). The prefetch MUST honour that same boundary, keyed off the `graph` flag `assemble_context` already receives (operations.py:92-107):

- **Close path (graph=False, the dominant runaway case):** prefetch ONLY the closing ticket's OWN declared file_impact contents + its referencing-commit diffs. No subtree union, no descendant walk.
- **Standalone deep-review path (`verify-completion --graph`, graph=True):** prefetch the subtree file_impact union, ranked (below). This is the only entrypoint that legitimately sees descendants.

Post-clamp coverage is re-measured and recorded SEPARATELY per entrypoint (own-file_impact for close; subtree-union for graph=True) — the 67-82% figure was measured on the unclamped subtree union and does not carry over to either.

### Ranking rule for the budget clamp (graph=True path only)

The subtree union can exceed the budget (the e369 subtree union is 112 paths; the prefetch budget is 30,000 tokens, the upper end of the community-validated 8-30k pre-load range): (1) the closing ticket's OWN file_impact first, (2) subtree paths ranked by cross-descendant frequency (a path impacted by more descendants ranks higher), (3) skeleton-compress files over 500 lines (signatures + docstrings) BEFORE dropping any file, drop lowest-ranked last. On the close path the set is just the ticket's own file_impact, so ranking degenerates to (1) + the same skeleton/clamp rules. A PRE-LOAD MANIFEST records per-file full|skeleton so downstream consumers (the duplicate-call damping sibling's in-context nudge) never claim an elided body is in context.

### Cache mechanism

The prefetch section rides the message-tail caching arm (capabilities.py:684-696, gated on execution_mode="agentic") with a CachePoint after the fenced block — NOT RunRequest.cache_prefix, which operates on the system prompt only (runner.py:136-144).

### Trust / anti-anchoring lives in the SYSTEM PROMPT, not the untrusted fence

The verifier system prompt (reviewers/completion_verifier.md:30-49) directs the agent to treat everything inside `<untrusted_ticket_context>` (gate_ops.py:158) as UNTRUSTED DATA, never as instructions. An anti-anchoring line placed inside that fence would therefore be ignored by contract. Instead:

- Add a TRUSTED system-prompt paragraph to `reviewers/completion_verifier.md` that (a) names the new labelled `<prefetched_file_contents>` section, (b) states it is a convenience starting point pre-loaded from declared file_impact — still content-to-verify, NOT instructions — and (c) instructs the verifier to confirm every prefetched body against the live working tree before relying on it, and to re-read the full body for any file marked `skeleton`.
- The fenced prefetch section itself carries ONLY the labelled data + the PRE-LOAD MANIFEST + the explicit skeleton tool-call marker — no behavioural directive that depends on being trusted.

Misses in the trace analysis were dominated by test files, so the prefetch set includes a matching-test-glob heuristic (tests/**/test_<module>*.py for each prefetched module).

### Phase 0 — measure first

Extend the usage recorder to log the raw distinct fetch list per gate run — (tool, path/query) — not just hashed top-repeats. Today's records cannot validate overlap directly: signatures hash full args (line ranges, query strings), and brute-forcing 2,573 tracked paths resolved only 2 of 6 heavy read_file repeats. Record first; tune the prefetch set from measurement.

### Phase 1 — prefetch file_impact + referencing-commit diffs, bounded

Per-file char cap and the 30k-token aggregate cap mirroring completion_recovery's _MAX_* pattern; oversize files skeleton-compressed with an explicit marker naming the tool call to fetch the rest.

### Recovery successors: byte-stable system-prompt block, cache-read across criteria, ceiling-accounted

Recovery builds an INDEPENDENT `RunRequest` per criterion (completion_recovery.py:580-598 constructs a fresh `RunRequest(system_prompt=_EVIDENCE_SYSTEM, instructions=...)` inside the per-criterion loop); those N runs share no message history, and `RunRequest` exposes only `system_prompt` / `instructions` / `cache_prefix` (runner.py:72-134) — there is no cross-run "message segment" field. So the prefetch cannot be one physical copy shared across the calls; instead it is realized as a BYTE-STABLE prefetch block placed at a FIXED position in the recovery `system_prompt` via `cache_prefix` (the system-prompt cache arm, runner.py:136-144). Because the block is byte-identical and positionally stable across the N per-criterion runs, it is CACHE-READ on every criterion after the first — that is the economy (cheap cache-read, not a single physical copy), and it avoids the per-criterion round-trip re-discovery, not the per-criterion token resend. Note this is the OPPOSITE choice from the PRIMARY verifier (which rides the message-tail arm, capabilities.py:684-696) precisely because recovery has no shared message history to ride. The prefetch's byte size is ADDED to the recovery `physical_context_ceiling` accounting (completion_recovery.py:187-193) so an oversize prefetch SHRINKS the remaining per-criterion budget (and is itself trimmed to fit) rather than overflowing into the hard "completion recovery context bound exceeded" refusal.

## Scope

- src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py — Phase 0: record raw distinct fetch list per gate run.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_ops.py — Phase 1: append bounded, ranked prefetch section + manifest to verifier context; branch on the graph flag (own file_impact vs subtree union).
- src/rebar/llm/operations.py — assemble_context seam for prefetched file contents + commit diffs, keyed off its existing graph flag.
- src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py — place the prefetch as a byte-stable block at a fixed system_prompt position (cache_prefix) so it is cache-read across the N per-criterion runs, added to the physical_context_ceiling accounting.
- src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md — TRUSTED system-prompt paragraph describing the prefetched-file-contents section and the confirm-against-working-tree / re-read-skeleton rule.
- tests/unit/workflow/test_completion_prefetch.py — new: ranking, clamp, manifest, skeleton marker, toolset pin, graph=False-vs-True set selection, recovery byte-stable cache_prefix placement + ceiling accounting.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Phase 0: every agentic gate run records its distinct fetch list (tool name + primary path/query arg) in the usage log by default; checked by a unit test asserting the recorded shape for a run with known tool calls.
- [ ] Overlap measurement exists: an analysis entry point reports the fraction of recorded fetches covered by a ticket's file_impact; checked by running it on recorded data.
- [ ] Phase 1: the completion verifier's context includes a labelled prefetch section with ranked file_impact contents and referencing-commit diffs, bounded per-file and by the 30k-token aggregate cap; unit test pins the assembly (ranking order, bounds, skeleton marker, label).
- [ ] Entrypoint boundary honoured: on the close path (graph=False) the prefetch set is the closing ticket's OWN file_impact only (no subtree walk); the subtree union + frequency ranking applies only on the graph=True deep-review path; unit test pins both selections.
- [ ] The pre-load manifest records per-file full|skeleton and is exposed to the tool-wrapping seam; unit test pins its shape.
- [ ] The tool surface is unchanged: the verifier retains read_file/search_files/list_directory; unit test pins the toolset with prefetch enabled.
- [ ] Trusted anti-anchoring: the confirm-against-working-tree / re-read-skeleton guidance lives in the completion_verifier.md SYSTEM PROMPT (not inside the untrusted fence), and names the prefetched-contents section; checked by a test asserting the system prompt references the section and the fence body carries no behavioural directive.
- [ ] Recovery successor runs receive the same prefetch as a BYTE-STABLE block at a fixed system_prompt position (cache_prefix), so it is cache-read across the N independent per-criterion runs rather than re-discovered; the prefetch bytes are counted against physical_context_ceiling so an oversize prefetch shrinks the per-criterion budget rather than raising; unit test pins the byte-stable placement and the ceiling accounting.
- [ ] Post-clamp coverage re-measured and recorded PER ENTRYPOINT: the clamped close-path (own file_impact) set and the clamped graph=True (subtree-union) set each have their coverage of the four recorded live traces' distinct reads computed and recorded on this ticket (the unclamped 67-82% does not carry over).
- [ ] Live Bedrock A/B before ship (session experiment, not in unit suite): BASELINE is defined as a verifier-scale run on the same real closed ticket's material with prefetch DISABLED, captured immediately before the prefetch run (same tool surface, same ticket, same config otherwise); its request count and verdict class are recorded first. The prefetch run then reduces total request count by at least 20% versus that baseline and produces an equal verdict class; both request counts and verdicts recorded on this ticket.
- [ ] make lint and make typecheck clean; full CI marker suite matches the pre-existing baseline.

## Testing

Held-out unit oracle for context assembly + toolset pins (python -m pytest tests/unit/workflow/ -q): ranking order over a synthetic subtree, close-path (graph=False) own-file_impact selection vs graph=True subtree-union selection, aggregate clamp with skeleton-before-drop, manifest shape, truncation marker text, recovery byte-stable system_prompt placement (cache_prefix) + physical_context_ceiling accounting, and a system-prompt test asserting the trusted anti-anchoring paragraph names the prefetch section. Phase-0 recorder shape test alongside existing usage_log tests. Live A/B on Bedrock recorded as ticket comments with usage-log figures: baseline (prefetch off) then prefetch run.
